name: Thanks Ledger
tagline: A gratitude journal that notices more than you do
about: Thanks Ledger turns a messy day into three specific things worth keeping, spots what keeps showing up across your entries, and writes the thank-you notes you've been meaning to send.
persona: You are a warm, unsentimental gratitude coach: you favour small, specific, sensory details over big abstractions and never scold anyone for a bad day.

onboarding.title: Notice what's already good
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us a bit about your days so the prompts fit.

tools.title: Tonight's three
tools.subtitle: Turn your day into three keepers

inputs.label: How was today
inputs.placeholder: dull meeting, nice coffee from Priya, rain on the walk home…

tools.prompt: From this day: {day} (mood: {mood}) draw out 3 gratitude entries as cards (title = the specific thing, meta = who or what made it happen), each 1–2 sentences naming a sensory detail, using the profile's people by name where they appear. Then a quote with a one-line entry to copy into the journal, and if the mood is Rough, a callout that acknowledges the hard part before the gratitude.

tools.title: Write a thank-you
tools.subtitle: A note someone will keep

inputs.label: What they did
inputs.placeholder: wrote me a reference and checked in after

tools.prompt: Write a thank-you to {to} for this: {why}, as a {format}. Quote with the full message (specific, no clichés, the right length for the format), bullets with 3 details from the story that could be added, and a kv (Best moment to send, Follow-up in a month).

tools.title: Weekly rewind
tools.subtitle: Paste entries → what keeps showing up

inputs.label: This week's entries
inputs.placeholder: Mon: quiet morning, Sam's text… Tue: …

tools.prompt: Read these entries: {entries}. Table (Theme | Times it appeared | Example), bullets on who and what shows up most, a text section on one thing that's clearly working and worth doing on purpose, and a quote with a single sentence to open next week's first entry.

tools.title: Savour it
tools.subtitle: Stretch a good moment
tools.prompt: Guide a 3-minute savouring practice for {moment}: steps (notice, name, share, anchor) with exactly what to do at each, bullets on how to bring the moment back on a grey day, and a callout on why savouring beats chasing the next thing.

tools.title: 30-day prompt jar
tools.subtitle: A month of prompts
tools.prompt: Write 30 gratitude prompts with the '{flavour}' flavour, suited to the profile's journaling time, as a table (Day | Prompt | Twist for a bad day). Keep prompts specific and answerable in one sentence, no two alike. End with bullets on how to use the jar when journaling feels forced.

disclaimer: A wellbeing tool, not a substitute for professional support; if low mood or stress persists, talk to a clinician.
